name: Joshua Rotenberg
body: I'm applying for the Procurement Technology Solutions Analyst role, and since the posting asks specifically which minimum qualifications I meet, I'll go through them directly rather than write around it.

Bachelor's degree: yes, B.A. from Colorado State University. Three years of experience with procurement software specifically: no, I don't have that. My systems background is 15+ years deep in CRM and marketing-automation platforms (GoHighLevel, HubSpot, Salesforce), not procure-to-pay or PeopleSoft. What does transfer directly is the actual shape of the job: I'm the person who configures a platform, troubleshoots it when it breaks, sits between business users and a vendor's support team, and documents it so the next person isn't starting from zero. That's been the real job at Solenzo and Birdeye, just on a different category of software.

AI-driven solutions supporting business operations: yes, and this is where I'm confident. I've built and run AI-driven automation systems for clients, including a prospect-scoring workflow that enrolled 180+ contacts, and a meaningful part of that work is translating a non-technical person's loosely-formed request into a precise, structured prompt an AI system can actually execute reliably and repeatably. That's close to what your posting describes under natural-language prompting and AI-enabled process support.
If a fast learner who's spent a career being the technical point of contact for systems he didn't build is worth the procurement-specific ramp-up, I'd like to talk.
